CHIEF COMPLAINT:

The patient returns for ongoing surveillance of endometrial hyperplasia and continued management of menstrual irregularities associated with polycystic ovary syndrome. She presents with ongoing concerns regarding fertility. She reports having a period only every 2–3 months for the past several years. When she does menstruate, the bleeding is often heavy and prolonged. She also notes increased facial hair and acne that have worsened in the last year. She and her partner have been trying to conceive for over a year without success. She denies headaches, visual changes, or galactorrhea.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Polycystic ovary syndrome (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Endometrial Hyperplasia (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Endometrial hyperplasia without atypia
- Primary infertility
- Hirsutism
- Acne vulgaris
- Oligomenorrhea

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Wisdom teeth extraction (age 18)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Metformin 1000 mg orally twice daily
- Medroxyprogesterone acetate 10 mg orally daily for 10 days monthly (cyclic)
- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet orally daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed age 45
- Maternal aunt: Endometrial cancer, diagnosed age 52
- Sister: Polycystic ovary syndrome
- Father: Hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: High school mathematics teacher.

VITAL SIGNS:
Her BMI is 33 kg/m²

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, she has terminal hair on the upper lip and chin, as well as moderate acne on her cheeks. Pelvic exam reveals no abnormalities.

LABORATORY DATA:
A urine pregnancy test is negative. Labs show mildly elevated serum testosterone, normal prolactin and TSH, and an increased LH/FSH ratio.

IMAGING:
Transvaginal ultrasound shows bilaterally enlarged ovaries with multiple small follicles arranged along the periphery.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
The patient is diagnosed with an endocrinologic condition contributing to anovulation.
